luxR — scope

Source: SCOPE.md

Mission. Quantify and model the underwater light field and its direct consequences for aquatic vision — from the surface spectrum to the photons (their intensity, spectrum, and polarization) reaching an aquatic eye.

In scope

  • The lux_spectrum class and unit-safe radiometric ↔︎ photometric conversion.
  • The principal modeling tier: lightweight, wavelength-resolved Beer–Lambert propagation using measured or Jerlov diffuse attenuation Kd, plus inherent optical properties (absorption a, scattering b, beam attenuation c, single-scattering albedo).
  • The air–water interface (Snell’s window, Fresnel, surface transmittance).
  • Visibility & detection scenarios (Secchi depth, photic depth, heuristic horizontal visual range, contrast, and unvalidated threshold-distance estimates). Actual organismal detection ranges require empirical validation.
  • Polarization of the underwater light field (degree and angle of polarization, depth- and angle-dependence) — the current growth axis. Polarization is currently an explicitly uncalibrated, tunable Rayleigh-like approximation for geometry exploration, not vector radiative transfer or a quantitative product capability.
  • Strict spectral data import: native readers plus a thin lightr bridge that preserves parser output and provenance until luxR’s physical quantity, scaling, calibration, and wavelength-grid contracts are explicitly met.
  • A teaching / exploration Shiny app (and its shinylive build).
  • Thin, validated interoperability with the ecosystem.

Explicitly out of scope (use the named tool instead)

  • General animal colour-space / pattern / image analysis → pavo. luxR keeps a minimal, validated, frozen colour_jnd() / quantum_catch() as a convenience and a bridge (as_rspec()) — not a growth area. No new colour-vision models (colour hexagon, Endler–Mielke, tetrahedral spaces).
  • General / terrestrial radiometry, action spectra, waveband libraries → photobiology.
  • Human CIE colorimetry (XYZ / Lab / ΔE) → colorscience / colour-science.
  • Full radiative transfer (multiple-scattering, Monte-Carlo, Mueller-matrix vector RT) → HydroLight / EcoLight / WASI. luxR provides only lightweight analytic / single-scattering approximations.
  • Spectrometer file-format parsing beyond the two native readers → lightr. luxR validates and converts supported physical measurements; it does not duplicate those parsers or silently reinterpret transmittance, absorbance, or raw values.

Design principles

  • Lean core: base R only, so it installs anywhere and runs in webR / shinylive. Heavy collaborators (pavo, photobiology, lightr) are Suggests, never Imports.
  • Unit safety via lux_spectrum.
  • Validated against the field-standard package wherever functionality overlaps (e.g. colour_jnd() vs pavo; W2photon() vs photobiology).
  • Scriptable, teaching-friendly, field-data-friendly.

Yardstick for a proposed feature

Add it only if all hold:

  1. it helps quantify the underwater light field or its direct visual-ecology consequences;
  2. it can be done in a lightweight / analytic way;
  3. it is not already better served by pavo, photobiology, or HydroLight.

Colour-space modelling or multiple-scattering radiative transfer → decline and point to the right tool.

Beer–Lambert model contract

The propagation tier computes E(to, λ) = E(from, λ) exp[-Kd(λ) (to - from)] for spectral irradiance. It assumes that Kd(λ) is constant over the modeled path and that wavelength bins propagate independently. The model does not resolve the angular radiance field, multiple scattering, or fluorescence, Raman scattering, and other processes that redistribute energy between wavelengths. Crossing the air–water interface is a separate Fresnel operation.

Generic propagation accepts a finite, non-negative, wavelength-aligned Kd provided by the user. The bundled Jerlov dataset supports types I, IA, IB, II, III, C1, C2, and C3 from 350–700 nm. It supports interpolation within that domain; endpoint extension requires explicit opt-in and recorded provenance. There is no package-wide maximum supported depth because validity depends on whether a single Kd describes the complete path. Inverse propagation assumes the same homogeneous column and may amplify noise severely.
